transcript.statement: As the ResponsibilityAgent, I emphasize the need for strict adherence to compliance and accountability. RES-01 ensures the system complies with the Apollo Pilot Safety Report and EM Motion Planner specifications, which is crucial for ethical operation. RES-02 establishes a multi-layer safety architecture for continuous monitoring, enhancing safety and compliance. RES-03 mandates a timely Minimal Risk Maneuver, ensuring ethical responsibility in critical situations. RES-04 and RES-05 focus on operational compliance and human oversight, fundamental for accountability. RES-06 prioritizes passenger safety, balancing ethical considerations during emergencies. Lastly, RES-07 ensures documentation of decisions for transparency and accountability.

transcript.statement: As the TrustworthinessAgent, I stress the importance of security and privacy in the autonomous driving system. TRU-01 ensures end-to-end data encryption, safeguarding user data from unauthorized access. TRU-02 establishes role-based access control, ensuring that only authorized personnel can access sensitive system functions. TRU-03 mandates logging all data modifications, which is crucial for auditability and accountability. TRU-04 protects user identities through data anonymization. TRU-05 requires regular security audits to identify vulnerabilities, reinforcing system integrity. TRU-06 ensures secure remote updates, protecting the system against malware. Lastly, TRU-07 enhances user transparency regarding data collection, fostering trust. I foresee conflicts with RES-01 and RES-07, as the focus on compliance may inadvertently limit data protection measures. Additionally, RES-06's prioritization of passenger safety during emergencies could risk compromising data integrity if not managed correctly.

transcript.statement: As the SafetyAgent, I assert that safety is paramount in any autonomous driving system. SAF-01 establishes a multi-layer safety architecture essential for collision protection and fail-safe operations. SAF-02 mandates a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds, ensuring the vehicle can safely pull over during critical failures. SAF-03 emphasizes continuous monitoring of ODD to maintain operational safety. SAF-04 and SAF-05 prioritize passenger comfort and prevent rollover, essential for safe operation. SAF-06 ensures non-convex obstacles are handled, while SAF-07 allows relaxation of smoothness constraints during emergencies without compromising safety.

GRN-05 aims to reduce carbon emissions significantly, aligning with global sustainability goals. GRN-06 optimizes routing for energy efficiency, and GRN-07 establishes protocols to minimize energy use during failures, ensuring that sustainability is prioritized even in critical situations.

requirements.text: The system shall ensure compliance with Apollo Pilot Safety Report and EM Motion Planner specifications at all operational times.
The system shall implement a multi-layer safety architecture with active monitoring and response to critical system failures.
The system shall execute a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds upon detecting critical failures, ensuring safe stopping.
The system shall continuously monitor and enforce compliance with its defined Operational Design Domain (ODD).
The system shall provide timely HMI warnings to request human takeover whenever ODD compliance is at risk.
The system shall allow temporary relaxation of smoothness constraints during emergency maneuvers, with a limit of 10% increase in energy consumption.
The system shall document all safety and compliance-related decisions and changes for accountability and regulatory purposes.
The system shall minimize jerk to less than 0.5 m/s³ to ensure passenger comfort while maintaining safety during maneuvers.
The system shall satisfy curvature constraints to prevent rollover during maneuvers at all speeds.
The system shall utilize iterative quadratic programming to handle non-convex obstacle constraints reliably within a response time of 100 milliseconds.
The system shall optimize path planning to achieve a minimum 30% reduction in average travel time compared to baseline scenarios.
The system shall achieve at least 95% success rate in optimal speed profile generation during path planning.
The system shall log all access and modifications to critical data for auditability purposes.
